newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb explodes in Algiers, many feared dead.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb explodes in Algiers, many feared dead.

text.p: A car bomb exploded near a coffee shop in central Algiers on Monday and many people were feared dead, eyewitnesses said.
The bomb went off at about 12.45 a.m. (1145 GMT) in a street near a crowded coffee shop, said the witnesses, speaking by telephone from Algiers.
"I saw much blood at the scene. I fear many people might have died," one said.
There was no immediate word on who was responsible.
Government forces have been locked in conflict for nearly five years with Moslem guerrillas trying to topple the North African country's secular leaders.
About 60,000 people, mostly Moslem militants and security forces members, have died since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election radical Islamists were set to win.
On August 1, a remote-controlled bomb killed French Roman Catholic bishop Pierre Claverie at his residence in the western city of Oran, hours after he met French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
Three days later a truck bomb wounded dozens in the central town of Tiaret, 225 km (140 miles) southwest of Algiers.
On August 6, a home-made bomb wounded five people in a restaurant in central Algiers and on August 8 a similar bomb on ripped through an Algiers coffee shop, wounding at least seven people.

On January 30, 1995, a suicide car bomb in central Algiers killed at least 42 people and wounded nearly 300. The Armed Islamic Group, the most ruthless of Algeria's fundamentalist guerrilla movements, claimed responsibility.
